subtype: Approach: explaining the pivot to the team openly [Action]
passage:
On Monday morning Uday pulled the whole team into the meeting room and put a sheet on the wall screen: monthly users, money in, money out, the line going the wrong way. "This is where we are," Uday said. "And this is what I want to change."
Then came a slide for each role. The mobile work would move to a clinic dashboard. Support and sales would sit together. Parul's testing job would grow to cover the new product, with the same pay and a new review date.
Parul asked three questions about the numbers and then nodded slowly. By Friday two engineers had handed in notice, politely and with thanks. Everyone else stayed and started on Monday's plan.

qa.q: What did Uday put on the wall screen at the start of the meeting?
qa.a: Uday put up a sheet of monthly users, money in and money out.

qa.q: What was Parul feeling during the meeting?
qa.a: Parul was wary at first and then steadier: asking three questions about the numbers and then nodding slowly shows the doubts were being answered.

qa.q: What could Uday do to help the two engineers who left?
qa.a: Uday could offer a fair handover period and a reference, so the departure is respectful and the team's work continues smoothly.

qa.q: How might the two engineers who left have seen the meeting?
qa.a: They probably respected the openness even though the new plan was not for them, since they left politely and with thanks.

grounding: The passage shows a founder sharing the numbers, reasons and each role's future openly, so that most of the team commits despite two departures.
